original_description: Sets the maintainer's standard for writing and reviewing committed Go tests (_test.go): the golden hierarchy of contract authority, go-doc-first design and review, Go-team snippets to imitate, references per scenario.
best_description: Sets the maintainer's standard for writing and reviewing committed Go tests (_test.go): the golden hierarchy of contract authority, go-doc-first design and review, Go-team snippets to imitate, references per scenario.
final_description: Use for anything involving Go `_test.go` files. Triggers: write or add tests for a Go package or symbol; review, critique, clean up, or consolidate existing Go tests (including "what would a reviewer say", "these tests smell", "too many test funcs"); judge whether a suite is well-shaped; turn tests into runnable Examples for pkgsite; build a conformance/testing harness so other implementations can prove they satisfy an interface; design a new Go package's API so it stays testable before code exists; make a hard-to-test package testable. Also load whenever you finish writing or changing Go code — committed tests are part of done, so don't wait for the word "test". Guidance covers test naming, table tests and subtests, fakes, fixtures, examples, synctest, and committed-versus-throwaway. Skip for non-Go test frameworks, doc comments alone, `go vet`/CI tooling failures, fuzz-crash debugging, and test-plan process docs.

history.description: Use when Go tests are the work: writing or adding tests for a package, reviewing or cleaning up existing `_test.go` files, judging whether a test suite is well-shaped, converting one-liner tests into runnable examples, building a conformance harness for an interface, or shaping a new package's API so it is testable before any code exists. Also load whenever you write or change Go code, since committed tests are part of finishing it — don't wait for the user to say "test". Covers test naming and structure, table tests and subtests, fakes and helpers, fixtures, examples, concurrency and time (synctest), and what belongs in a committed test versus a throwaway one. Not for non-Go test frameworks, CI/tooling failures unrelated to test design, standalone doc-comment writing, fuzz-crash triage, or process/test-plan documents.
